In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Environment

 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	上一讲（u4-l1）我们看到 `UniSeg3D.loss()` 的十步前向里，点云先被 `collate()` 体素化为稀疏张量，再交给 `extract_feat()` 提取特征。本讲钻进这个「特征提取」的黑盒，读完你应该能：

11	
12	## 2. 前置知识
13	
14	### 2.1 为什么需要「稀疏」卷积
15	
16	3D 点云体素化之后几乎总是空的。以本项目的设置为例：`voxel_size=0.02`（2 厘米一个体素），一个 5m×5m×2.5m 的房间会被划成约 \( 250 \times 250 \times 125 \approx 7.8 \times 10^6 \) 个体素，而真实被点云占据的通常只有 \( 10^5 \) 量级：
17	
18	\[
19	\text{占用率} = \frac{N_{\text{占据体素}}}{N_{\text{总体素}}} \approx 1\%
20	\]
21	
22	如果直接用稠密 3D 卷积，99% 的乘加都花在空气上。**稀疏卷积**（sparse convolution）只对「有值的活跃位置」做计算：它预先算出卷积核窗口内哪些输入活跃点会影响哪些输出活跃点，生成一张「规则表」（rulebook，即索引对），然后只对这些配对执行稠密的小矩阵乘法。spconv 是 NVIDIA 开源的稀疏卷积库，本项目用它的 PyTorch 前端 `spconv.pytorch`。
23	
24	### 2.2 SparseConvTensor：稀疏世界的「张量」
25	
26	spconv 不用 `(B,C,D,H,W)` 的稠密形状，而是用四元组描述一个稀疏张量：
27	
28	| 组成 | 形状 | 含义 |
29	| --- | --- | --- |
30	| `features` | `(N, C)` | N 个活跃体素的特征，按行排 |
31	| `indices` | `(N, 4)` | 每行是 `[batch_idx, x, y, z]`，指明该特征放在哪个体素格子里 |
32	| `spatial_shape` | `(3,)` | 网格逻辑大小 `[D, H, W]`（只用于越界检查，不代表真的开辟了这么大数组） |
33	| `batch_size` | 标量 | 批大小，配合 `batch_idx` 区分样本 |
34	
35	在 `uniseg3d.py` 的 `loss()` 里能看到它的构造现场：[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L453-L454](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L453-L454)——`features` 与 `coordinates` 来自 `collate()`（其中特征是「RGB + 质心中心化坐标」拼接出的 6 维，见 [uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L394-L403](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L394-L403)），这也是模型配置里 `in_channels=6` 的出处。
36	
37	### 2.3 三种卷积层与 indice_key
38	
39	本讲源码会用到 spconv 的三种层，行为差异是理解 U-Net 的关键：
40	
41	| 层 | 作用 | 活跃点集合 | 在本讲中的角色 |
42	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
43	| `SubMConv3d`（submanifold，流形保持） | 同分辨率卷积 | **完全不变**：输出位置 = 输入位置 | 堆叠特征、不改变网格 |
44	| `SparseConv3d`（可带 stride） | 下采样卷积 | 变化：滑动窗口扫描产生新的输出活跃点 | 每级一次 k=2、s=2 的减半下采样 |
45	| `SparseInverseConv3d` | 上采样「逆卷积」 | **精确还原**配对下采样层的输入活跃点 | 每级一次上采样，回到原网格 |
46	
47	**indice_key 机制**：spconv 为每个卷积层预计算输入→输出的索引对（rulebook）。如果两个层拥有相同的 `indice_key` 且输入活跃点集合一致，它们可以**复用同一张规则表**，省掉重复的索引计算。这就是为什么源码里同级的一摞 `SubMConv3d` 都标着 `subm{i}`。更重要的是：`SparseInverseConv3d` 自己不算卷积映射，它直接**转置复用**同 key 的 `SparseConv3d` 已经算好的索引对——所以它必须和下采样层共用同一个 `indice_key`（如 `spconv{i}`），且 `kernel_size` 必须一致（都是 2），输出活跃点也因此精确落在下采样前的体素集合上。这个「精确还原」性质是后文跳连拼接能逐行对齐的前提。
48

51	- **U-Net**：编码器逐级下采样（视野变大、体素变少、通道变多），解码器逐级上采样还原图分辨率，并把编码器同级的特征**跳连拼接**（skip connection）给解码器，兼顾「语义深」与「定位准」。

76	\]

78	- **恒等分支 `i_branch`**：通道不变时就是 `nn.Identity`；通道变化时退化为 1×1×1 的 `SubMConv3d` 做逐点线性投影（因为 `SubMConv3d` kernel_size=1 时活跃点也不变）。

138	### 4.2 SpConvUNet 的递归构建：`__init__` 与通道数推算
139	
140	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
141	
142	`SpConvUNet` 最特别的地方是**用自己构造自己**：它的 `__init__` 在 `len(num_planes) > 1` 时会 `new` 一个通道表更短的 `SpConvUNet` 存进 `self.u`，如此剥洋葱直到只剩一个平面（最深层）。也就是说，`num_planes=[32,64,96,128,160]` 的五级 U-Net 其实是五个嵌套的 `SpConvUNet` 实例，每一级处理一个分辨率。每级五件套：
143	
144	| 部件 | 类型 | 通道 |
145	| --- | --- | --- |
146	| `blocks` | `block_reps`(=2) 个 `ResidualBlock` | `C → C` |
147	| `conv` | `SparseConv3d` k=2 s=2（pre-norm 前置 Norm+ReLU） | `C → C_next`（下采样） |
148	| `u` | 递归子 `SpConvUNet` | 处理 `num_planes[1:]` |
149	| `deconv` | `SparseInverseConv3d` k=2（与 conv 同 key） | `C_next → C`（上采样） |
150	| `blocks_tail` | 2 个 `ResidualBlock` | `2C → C`、`C → C`（精炼拼接特征） |
151	
152	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
153	
154	```
155	SpConvUNet(num_planes=[32,64,96,128,160], indice_key_id=1)
156	 ├─ blocks      : 2×ResidualBlock(32→32,  key='subm1')
157	 ├─ conv        : SparseConv3d(32→64,  k=2,s=2, key='spconv1')
158	 ├─ u = SpConvUNet([64,96,128,160], indice_key_id=2)
159	 │    ├─ blocks : 2×RB(64→64, 'subm2'); conv: 64→96 ('spconv2')
160	 │    ├─ u = SpConvUNet([96,128,160], id=3)
161	 │    │    └─ ... 继续递归 ...
162	 │    │         SpConvUNet([160], id=5)：只有 blocks(2×RB 160→160)，无 conv/deconv/tail
163	 │    └─ deconv : SparseInverseConv3d(96→64, key='spconv2'); tail: 128→64, 64→64
164	 └─ deconv      : SparseInverseConv3d(64→32, key='spconv1'); tail: 64→32, 32→32
165	```
166	
167	通道数推算只需三条规则（设本级通道 \( C \)，级编号从 1 开始，stride 2 每级减半分辨率，第 \( \ell \) 级体素边长 \( = 0.02 \times 2^{\ell-1} \) 米）：
168	
169	1. `blocks`：`C → C`，重复 `block_reps` 次；
170	2. `conv`/`deconv`：`C → C'` 与 `C' → C`，`indice_key` 分别为 `spconv{级号}`，deconv 与 conv 同 key；
171	3. `blocks_tail`：第 `i` 个块输入通道是 `num_planes[0] * (2 - i)`（`i=0,1`），即先吃「恒等 \( C \) + 上采样 \( C \) = \( 2C \)」的拼接，再 `C → C`。
172	
173	五级完整通道表：
174	
175	| 级 | subm key | blocks（×2） | conv 下采样 | deconv 上采样 | blocks_tail |
176	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
177	| 1 | subm1 | 32→32 | 32→64 (spconv1) | 64→32 (spconv1) | 64→32, 32→32 |
178	| 2 | subm2 | 64→64 | 64→96 (spconv2) | 96→64 | 128→64, 64→64 |
179	| 3 | subm3 | 96→96 | 96→128 (spconv3) | 128→96 | 192→96, 96→96 |
180	| 4 | subm4 | 128→128 | 128→160 (spconv4) | 160→128 | 256→128, 128→128 |
181	| 5 | subm5 | 160→160 | —（最深层） | — | — |
182	
183	另外，第 1 级的 `subm1` 与主模型 `input_conv` 的 `indice_key='subm1'` 相同（见 4.4），两者输入活跃点一致，可共享规则表。

252	### 4.3 SpConvUNet 前向：下采样、跳连拼接与 return_blocks
253	
254	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
255	
256	`forward` 描述每一级「下去—上来—拼—精炼」的四步；`return_blocks` 决定是否把**每级的最终输出**收集成一个列表一起返回。本项目的配置打开了 `return_blocks=True`，所以 `extract_feat` 里写的是 `x, _ = self.unet(x)`——第二个返回值 `previous_outputs` 被丢弃，模型实际只消费最细层（32 通道）输出，超点查询全部从这一层聚合（呼应 u4-l1 的「超点即查询」）。这个开关源自 SPFormer 的多尺度用法，UniSeg3D 保留了它但只用单尺度。
257	
258	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
259	
260	```
261	forward(x, previous_outputs=None):
262	 1. output = blocks(x)                      # 本级精炼（活跃点不变）
263	 2. identity = output 的浅拷贝包装          # 跳连备用
264	 3. 若还有更深层：
265	    a. output_decoder = conv(output)        # 下采样，体素数减少
266	    b. output_decoder, previous_outputs = u(output_decoder, previous_outputs)  # 递归
267	    c. output_decoder = deconv(output_decoder)  # 上采样，精确还原到本级活跃点
268	    d. output = replace_feature(cat(identity.features, output_decoder.features, dim=1))  # 跳连拼接 → 2C 通道
269	    e. output = blocks_tail(output)         # 2C → C → C
270	 4. 若 return_blocks：previous_outputs.append(output)；返回 (output, previous_outputs)
271	    否则只返回 output
272	```
273	
274	关键不变量：`deconv` 输出的活跃点集合与 `identity` 完全一致（`SparseInverseConv3d` 精确求逆），所以第 d 步可以**逐行** `torch.cat`——两边的第 k 行描述的是同一个体素。这也是 4.1.3 中残差相加、此处通道拼接能直接对齐的根本原因。

317	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
318	
319	`SpConvUNet` 的第一级通道是 32，而体素特征只有 6 维（RGB + 中心化坐标）；网络的最外层还需要一个「入口卷积」把 6 维升到 32 维，以及一个「出口归一化」在 U-Net 输出后做 BatchNorm + ReLU。这两件小事不属于 U-Net 本体，由主模型 `UniSeg3D` 的 `_init_layers` 直接用 spconv 层搭成：
320	
321	- `input_conv`：`SubMConv3d(6 → 32, k=3, indice_key='subm1')`，与第 1 级 blocks 共享 `subm1` 规则表（两者输入活跃点一致）。
322	- `output_layer`：`BatchNorm1d(32) → ReLU`，纯特征级操作，不动稀疏结构。
323	
324	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
325	
326	```
327	extract_feat(x, superpoints, inverse_mapping, batch_offsets):
328	 1. x = input_conv(x)            # (N, 6) → (N, 32)，活跃点不变
329	 2. x, _ = unet(x)               # 五级 U-Net，输出最细层 (N, 32)
330	 3. x = output_layer(x)          # BN + ReLU
331	 4. feats = scatter_mean(x.features[inverse_mapping], superpoints)   # 体素 → 超点均值聚合
332	 5. 按 batch_offsets 切成每个场景一份，返回 List[Tensor]
333	```
334	
335	第 4-5 步在 u4-l1 已精读（`inverse_mapping` 把超点映射回其来源体素，`batch_offsets` 处理批内超点 id 全局偏移），本讲只需记住：**骨干只负责「体素级 32 维特征」，超点查询是在这之后的聚合产物**。
336	
337	#### 4.4.3 源码精读
338	
339	**入口/出口层的定义**：[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L345-L356](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L345-L356)——`input_conv` 是带 `indice_key='subm1'` 的 3³ `SubMConv3d`（`in_channels`/`num_channels` 分别来自配置 [L23-L24](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/configs/uniseg3d_1xb4_scannet_scanrefer_scannet200_unified.py#L23-L24) 的 6 与 32）；`output_layer` 是 `torch.nn.BatchNorm1d(32, eps=1e-4, momentum=0.1) + ReLU`，超参和 `ResidualBlock` 的 `norm_fn` 保持一致。
340	
341	**三步串联与超点聚合**：[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L358-L379](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L358-L379)——[L372-L374](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L372-L374) 依次过 `input_conv → unet → output_layer`；[L375](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L375) 用 `scatter_mean(x.features[inverse_mapping], superpoints)` 把体素特征按超点做均值池化；[L376-L378](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L376-L378) 按 `batch_offsets` 切回逐场景列表。
342	
343	一个值得留意的分工细节：稀疏张量的**坐标/特征准备**用的是 MinkowskiEngine（`collate()` 里 `ME.TensorField` 与 `ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate`，[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L394-L411](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L394-L411)），而**卷积骨干**跑在 spconv 上（[L453-L454](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L453-L454) 构造 `spconv.SparseConvTensor`）。两个库各干各的活，靠 `(indices, features)` 这份共同语言衔接。
344	
345	#### 4.4.4 代码实践
346	
347	1. **实践目标**：亲手复现 `extract_feat` 的前三步（不含超点聚合），确认外壳与 U-Net 通道严丝合缝。
348	2. **操作步骤**（示例代码）：
349	
350	```python
351	import torch, spconv.pytorch as spconv
352	from uniseg3d.spconv_unet import SpConvUNet
353	
354	# 手工搭外壳（与 _init_layers 中的定义逐项等价，避免实例化整个 UniSeg3D）：
355	input_conv = spconv.SparseSequential(spconv.SubMConv3d(
356	    6, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1, bias=False, indice_key='subm1'))
357	output_layer = spconv.SparseSequential(
358	    torch.nn.BatchNorm1d(32, eps=1e-4, momentum=0.1), torch.nn.ReLU(inplace=True))
359	
360	N = 5000
361	feats = torch.randn(N, 6)
362	idx = torch.cat([torch.zeros(N, 1, dtype=torch.int32),
363	                 torch.randint(0, 100, (N, 3), dtype=torch.int32)], dim=1)
364	x = spconv.SparseConvTensor(feats, idx, [100, 100, 100], batch_size=1)
365	
366	unet = SpConvUNet([32 * (i + 1) for i in range(5)], return_blocks=True)
367	with torch.no_grad():
368	    h, _ = unet(input_conv(x))
369	    h = output_layer(h)
370	print('体素级特征:', tuple(h.features.shape))   # 期望 (5000, 32)
371	```
372	
373	3. **需要观察的现象**：`input_conv` 后通道变 32、体素数不变；U-Net 输出仍为 `(5000, 32)`；`output_layer` 只改数值不改形状。
374	4. **预期结果**：最终打印 `(5000, 32)`，与 `extract_feat` 在 [uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L374](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L374) 处得到的张量规格一致。**待本地验证**。
375	
376	#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案
377	
378	1. **练习**：`input_conv` 为什么选 `SubMConv3d` 而不是 `SparseConv3d`？
379	   **答案**：入口卷积只做 6→32 的通道升维，不应改变活跃点集合；`SubMConv3d` 保证输出位置与输入一致，后续 U-Net 第 1 级（以及共享的 `subm1` 规则表）才能在同一网格上工作。`SparseConv3d` 会做窗口扫描、改变活跃点集合，破坏这种对齐。
380	2. **练习**：如果把配置的 `num_channels` 从 32 改成 64，需要同步改动哪些地方才能保证前向不报错？
381	   **答案**：`num_planes` 由 `num_channels` 推导（配置 L37），U-Net 内部自动变宽；但 `output_layer` 的 `BatchNorm1d(num_channels)`、解码器侧消费的查询维度（`UnifiedQueryDecoder` 的 `in_channels`/`d_model` 相关设置）以及 `type_embedding` 的 `num_channels` 都依赖同一变量，而预训练权重（如 SSTNet `load_from`）的通道布局也须匹配——这正是配置用变量 `num_channels` 统一推导、而不是散落硬编码的原因。
382	3. **练习**：`output_layer` 里的 `BatchNorm1d(32)` 与 `ResidualBlock` 里的 `norm_fn` 有何异同？
383	   **答案**：都是对 `(N, C)` 的体素特征按通道归一化，超参一致（eps=1e-4, momentum=0.1）；区别只是定义位置——前者是主模型出口处的裸 `torch.nn.BatchNorm1d`，后者是作为 `functools.partial` 构造器贯穿所有残差块的默认 `norm_fn`。
384	
385	## 5. 综合实践
386	
387	**任务：为五级 SpConvUNet 绘制完整的「通道—体素数」数据流表，并验证递归自相似与外壳衔接。**

391	3. 再分别用 `num_planes=[32,64,96]` 与 `[32,64]` 重跑，确认表格结构按同一模式缩短（证明递归自相似），且最细层输出始终是 `(N, 32)`。
392	4. 最后套上 4.4.4 的 `input_conv`/`output_layer` 外壳，核对从 `(N, 6)` 进到 `(N, 32)` 出的完整链路，与 `extract_feat`（[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L372-L374](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L372-L374)）的调用顺序一致。

394	
395	## 6. 本讲小结
396	
397	- `ResidualBlock` 是 pre-norm 残差块：`Norm → ReLU → SubMConv3d(3³) → Norm → ReLU → SubMConv3d(3³)` 加恒等分支（通道不等时用 1³ `SubMConv3d` 投影），全程不改变活跃点集合。

401	- 外壳 `input_conv`（`SubMConv3d` 6→32，共享 `subm1`）与 `output_layer`（BN+ReLU）由主模型 `_init_layers` 搭建；体素级 32 维特征再经 `scatter_mean` 聚合成超点查询——「超点即查询」的原料在此产出。

# 稀疏卷积骨干 SpConvUNet

## 1. 本讲目标

上一讲（u4-l1）我们看到 `UniSeg3D.loss()` 的十步前向里，点云先被 `collate()` 体素化为稀疏张量，再交给 `extract_feat()` 提取特征。本讲钻进这个「特征提取」的黑盒，读完你应该能：

1. 理解 spconv 的稀疏张量 `SparseConvTensor` 与 `indice_key` 机制——为什么共享同一个 key 能省计算、为什么上采样层必须和下采样层配对。
2. 掌握 `ResidualBlock` 的 pre-norm 残差结构（`SubMConv3d` + 归一化前置）。
3. 掌握 `SpConvUNet` 的**递归构建**方式：`num_planes=[32,64,96,128,160]` 五级 U-Net 是由同一个类自我嵌套出来的，并能手工推算每一层的通道数。
4. 理解 `input_conv` / `output_layer` 外壳如何把 6 通道原始特征接入 U-Net、又把 32 通道体素特征交还给 `extract_feat` 做超点聚合。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 为什么需要「稀疏」卷积

3D 点云体素化之后几乎总是空的。以本项目的设置为例：`voxel_size=0.02`（2 厘米一个体素），一个 5m×5m×2.5m 的房间会被划成约 \( 250 \times 250 \times 125 \approx 7.8 \times 10^6 \) 个体素，而真实被点云占据的通常只有 \( 10^5 \) 量级：

\[
\text{占用率} = \frac{N_{\text{占据体素}}}{N_{\text{总体素}}} \approx 1\%
\]

如果直接用稠密 3D 卷积，99% 的乘加都花在空气上。**稀疏卷积**（sparse convolution）只对「有值的活跃位置」做计算：它预先算出卷积核窗口内哪些输入活跃点会影响哪些输出活跃点，生成一张「规则表」（rulebook，即索引对），然后只对这些配对执行稠密的小矩阵乘法。spconv 是 NVIDIA 开源的稀疏卷积库，本项目用它的 PyTorch 前端 `spconv.pytorch`。

### 2.2 SparseConvTensor：稀疏世界的「张量」

spconv 不用 `(B,C,D,H,W)` 的稠密形状，而是用四元组描述一个稀疏张量：

| 组成 | 形状 | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `features` | `(N, C)` | N 个活跃体素的特征，按行排 |
| `indices` | `(N, 4)` | 每行是 `[batch_idx, x, y, z]`，指明该特征放在哪个体素格子里 |
| `spatial_shape` | `(3,)` | 网格逻辑大小 `[D, H, W]`（只用于越界检查，不代表真的开辟了这么大数组） |
| `batch_size` | 标量 | 批大小，配合 `batch_idx` 区分样本 |

在 `uniseg3d.py` 的 `loss()` 里能看到它的构造现场：[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L453-L454](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L453-L454)——`features` 与 `coordinates` 来自 `collate()`（其中特征是「RGB + 质心中心化坐标」拼接出的 6 维，见 [uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L394-L403](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L394-L403)），这也是模型配置里 `in_channels=6` 的出处。

### 2.3 三种卷积层与 indice_key

本讲源码会用到 spconv 的三种层，行为差异是理解 U-Net 的关键：

| 层 | 作用 | 活跃点集合 | 在本讲中的角色 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SubMConv3d`（submanifold，流形保持） | 同分辨率卷积 | **完全不变**：输出位置 = 输入位置 | 堆叠特征、不改变网格 |
| `SparseConv3d`（可带 stride） | 下采样卷积 | 变化：滑动窗口扫描产生新的输出活跃点 | 每级一次 k=2、s=2 的减半下采样 |
| `SparseInverseConv3d` | 上采样「逆卷积」 | **精确还原**配对下采样层的输入活跃点 | 每级一次上采样，回到原网格 |

**indice_key 机制**：spconv 为每个卷积层预计算输入→输出的索引对（rulebook）。如果两个层拥有相同的 `indice_key` 且输入活跃点集合一致，它们可以**复用同一张规则表**，省掉重复的索引计算。这就是为什么源码里同级的一摞 `SubMConv3d` 都标着 `subm{i}`。更重要的是：`SparseInverseConv3d` 自己不算卷积映射，它直接**转置复用**同 key 的 `SparseConv3d` 已经算好的索引对——所以它必须和下采样层共用同一个 `indice_key`（如 `spconv{i}`），且 `kernel_size` 必须一致（都是 2），输出活跃点也因此精确落在下采样前的体素集合上。这个「精确还原」性质是后文跳连拼接能逐行对齐的前提。

### 2.4 U-Net 与 pre-norm 残差

- **U-Net**：编码器逐级下采样（视野变大、体素变少、通道变多），解码器逐级上采样还原图分辨率，并把编码器同级的特征**跳连拼接**（skip connection）给解码器，兼顾「语义深」与「定位准」。
- **pre-norm 残差**：残差块写作 `y = x + F(Norm(x))`，即先归一化再进卷积分支（对应 `normalize_before=True`）；相对 post-norm（先卷积后归一化），它让梯度可以沿恒等通路无阻碍回传，是 Transformer 时代流行的做法。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲关注点 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [uniseg3d/spconv_unet.py](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/spconv_unet.py#L1-L237) | 稀疏卷积骨干（改自 SPFormer） | `ResidualBlock` 与 `SpConvUNet` 全部实现，共 237 行 |
| [uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L311-L379) | 主模型 | 骨干的组装（L311）、`input_conv`/`output_layer` 外壳（L345-L356）、`extract_feat`（L358-L379） |
| [configs/uniseg3d_1xb4_scannet_scanrefer_scannet200_unified.py](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/configs/uniseg3d_1xb4_scannet_scanrefer_scannet200_unified.py#L20-L38) | 主配置 | `num_channels=32`、`in_channels=6`、`backbone` 的 `num_planes` 与 `return_blocks` |

配置中的骨干设定（注意 `num_planes` 是一个推导式）：

[configs/uniseg3d_1xb4_scannet_scanrefer_scannet200_unified.py:L35-L38](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/configs/uniseg3d_1xb4_scannet_scanrefer_scannet200_unified.py#L35-L38)——`num_planes=[num_channels * (i + 1) for i in range(5)]`，配合 [L9](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/configs/uniseg3d_1xb4_scannet_scanrefer_scannet200_unified.py#L9) 的 `num_channels = 32`，即 `[32, 64, 96, 128, 160]`，并打开 `return_blocks=True`。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 ResidualBlock：pre-norm 残差块

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`ResidualBlock` 是 U-Net 每一级的基本积木，做的是「同分辨率特征精炼」：输入输出活跃点完全相同（全部用 `SubMConv3d`），通道数可以变。它是一条标准的残差结构：

\[
y = \mathrm{Branch}_I(x) + \mathrm{Branch}_{conv}(x)
\]

- **恒等分支 `i_branch`**：通道不变时就是 `nn.Identity`；通道变化时退化为 1×1×1 的 `SubMConv3d` 做逐点线性投影（因为 `SubMConv3d` kernel_size=1 时活跃点也不变）。
- **卷积分支 `conv_branch`**：两层 3×3×3 `SubMConv3d`，pre-norm 模式下每个卷积前先 `Norm → ReLU`。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```
输入 SparseConvTensor x (N, C_in)
├── identity = 只包一层的新 SparseConvTensor（共享 features/indices）
├── h = conv_branch(x)：  Norm → ReLU → SubMConv3d(3³) → Norm → ReLU → SubMConv3d(3³)
├── id = i_branch(identity)： Identity 或 SubMConv3d(1³)
└── 输出 = h.replace_feature(h.features + id.features)   # 逐体素相加，(N, C_out)
```

注意 spconv 的张量「不可原地改特征」：相加结果要用 `replace_feature` 装回一个新 `SparseConvTensor`。

### 4.2 SpConvUNet 的递归构建：`__init__` 与通道数推算

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`SpConvUNet` 最特别的地方是**用自己构造自己**：它的 `__init__` 在 `len(num_planes) > 1` 时会 `new` 一个通道表更短的 `SpConvUNet` 存进 `self.u`，如此剥洋葱直到只剩一个平面（最深层）。也就是说，`num_planes=[32,64,96,128,160]` 的五级 U-Net 其实是五个嵌套的 `SpConvUNet` 实例，每一级处理一个分辨率。每级五件套：

| 部件 | 类型 | 通道 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `blocks` | `block_reps`(=2) 个 `ResidualBlock` | `C → C` |
| `conv` | `SparseConv3d` k=2 s=2（pre-norm 前置 Norm+ReLU） | `C → C_next`（下采样） |
| `u` | 递归子 `SpConvUNet` | 处理 `num_planes[1:]` |
| `deconv` | `SparseInverseConv3d` k=2（与 conv 同 key） | `C_next → C`（上采样） |
| `blocks_tail` | 2 个 `ResidualBlock` | `2C → C`、`C → C`（精炼拼接特征） |

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```
SpConvUNet(num_planes=[32,64,96,128,160], indice_key_id=1)
 ├─ blocks      : 2×ResidualBlock(32→32,  key='subm1')
 ├─ conv        : SparseConv3d(32→64,  k=2,s=2, key='spconv1')
 ├─ u = SpConvUNet([64,96,128,160], indice_key_id=2)
 │    ├─ blocks : 2×RB(64→64, 'subm2'); conv: 64→96 ('spconv2')
 │    ├─ u = SpConvUNet([96,128,160], id=3)
 │    │    └─ ... 继续递归 ...
 │    │         SpConvUNet([160], id=5)：只有 blocks(2×RB 160→160)，无 conv/deconv/tail
 │    └─ deconv : SparseInverseConv3d(96→64, key='spconv2'); tail: 128→64, 64→64
 └─ deconv      : SparseInverseConv3d(64→32, key='spconv1'); tail: 64→32, 32→32
```

通道数推算只需三条规则（设本级通道 \( C \)，级编号从 1 开始，stride 2 每级减半分辨率，第 \( \ell \) 级体素边长 \( = 0.02 \times 2^{\ell-1} \) 米）：

1. `blocks`：`C → C`，重复 `block_reps` 次；
2. `conv`/`deconv`：`C → C'` 与 `C' → C`，`indice_key` 分别为 `spconv{级号}`，deconv 与 conv 同 key；
3. `blocks_tail`：第 `i` 个块输入通道是 `num_planes[0] * (2 - i)`（`i=0,1`），即先吃「恒等 \( C \) + 上采样 \( C \) = \( 2C \)」的拼接，再 `C → C`。

五级完整通道表：

| 级 | subm key | blocks（×2） | conv 下采样 | deconv 上采样 | blocks_tail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | subm1 | 32→32 | 32→64 (spconv1) | 64→32 (spconv1) | 64→32, 32→32 |
| 2 | subm2 | 64→64 | 64→96 (spconv2) | 96→64 | 128→64, 64→64 |
| 3 | subm3 | 96→96 | 96→128 (spconv3) | 128→96 | 192→96, 96→96 |
| 4 | subm4 | 128→128 | 128→160 (spconv4) | 160→128 | 256→128, 128→128 |
| 5 | subm5 | 160→160 | —（最深层） | — | — |

另外，第 1 级的 `subm1` 与主模型 `input_conv` 的 `indice_key='subm1'` 相同（见 4.4），两者输入活跃点一致，可共享规则表。

### 4.3 SpConvUNet 前向：下采样、跳连拼接与 return_blocks

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`forward` 描述每一级「下去—上来—拼—精炼」的四步；`return_blocks` 决定是否把**每级的最终输出**收集成一个列表一起返回。本项目的配置打开了 `return_blocks=True`，所以 `extract_feat` 里写的是 `x, _ = self.unet(x)`——第二个返回值 `previous_outputs` 被丢弃，模型实际只消费最细层（32 通道）输出，超点查询全部从这一层聚合（呼应 u4-l1 的「超点即查询」）。这个开关源自 SPFormer 的多尺度用法，UniSeg3D 保留了它但只用单尺度。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```
forward(x, previous_outputs=None):
 1. output = blocks(x)                      # 本级精炼（活跃点不变）
 2. identity = output 的浅拷贝包装          # 跳连备用
 3. 若还有更深层：
    a. output_decoder = conv(output)        # 下采样，体素数减少
    b. output_decoder, previous_outputs = u(output_decoder, previous_outputs)  # 递归
    c. output_decoder = deconv(output_decoder)  # 上采样，精确还原到本级活跃点
    d. output = replace_feature(cat(identity.features, output_decoder.features, dim=1))  # 跳连拼接 → 2C 通道
    e. output = blocks_tail(output)         # 2C → C → C
 4. 若 return_blocks：previous_outputs.append(output)；返回 (output, previous_outputs)
    否则只返回 output
```

关键不变量：`deconv` 输出的活跃点集合与 `identity` 完全一致（`SparseInverseConv3d` 精确求逆），所以第 d 步可以**逐行** `torch.cat`——两边的第 k 行描述的是同一个体素。这也是 4.1.3 中残差相加、此处通道拼接能直接对齐的根本原因。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**本级 blocks 与跳连快照**：[uniseg3d/spconv_unet.py:L211-L214](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/spconv_unet.py#L211-L214)——`output` 先过 `blocks`，再用其 `features/indices/spatial_shape/batch_size` 包装出 `identity`。

2. **练习**：`previous_outputs` 里的元素顺序为什么是「由深到浅」而不是「由浅到深」？
   **答案**：`append` 发生在各级 `forward` 的**末尾**，而递归调用 `self.u(...)` 发生在各级的中段；最深层最先执行到末尾，最先 append，外层后 append，故列表由深到浅排列。

### 4.4 外壳：input_conv / output_layer 与 extract_feat

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

`SpConvUNet` 的第一级通道是 32，而体素特征只有 6 维（RGB + 中心化坐标）；网络的最外层还需要一个「入口卷积」把 6 维升到 32 维，以及一个「出口归一化」在 U-Net 输出后做 BatchNorm + ReLU。这两件小事不属于 U-Net 本体，由主模型 `UniSeg3D` 的 `_init_layers` 直接用 spconv 层搭成：

- `input_conv`：`SubMConv3d(6 → 32, k=3, indice_key='subm1')`，与第 1 级 blocks 共享 `subm1` 规则表（两者输入活跃点一致）。
- `output_layer`：`BatchNorm1d(32) → ReLU`，纯特征级操作，不动稀疏结构。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```
extract_feat(x, superpoints, inverse_mapping, batch_offsets):
 1. x = input_conv(x)            # (N, 6) → (N, 32)，活跃点不变
 2. x, _ = unet(x)               # 五级 U-Net，输出最细层 (N, 32)
 3. x = output_layer(x)          # BN + ReLU
 4. feats = scatter_mean(x.features[inverse_mapping], superpoints)   # 体素 → 超点均值聚合
 5. 按 batch_offsets 切成每个场景一份，返回 List[Tensor]
```

第 4-5 步在 u4-l1 已精读（`inverse_mapping` 把超点映射回其来源体素，`batch_offsets` 处理批内超点 id 全局偏移），本讲只需记住：**骨干只负责「体素级 32 维特征」，超点查询是在这之后的聚合产物**。

#### 4.4.3 源码精读

**入口/出口层的定义**：[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L345-L356](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L345-L356)——`input_conv` 是带 `indice_key='subm1'` 的 3³ `SubMConv3d`（`in_channels`/`num_channels` 分别来自配置 [L23-L24](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/configs/uniseg3d_1xb4_scannet_scanrefer_scannet200_unified.py#L23-L24) 的 6 与 32）；`output_layer` 是 `torch.nn.BatchNorm1d(32, eps=1e-4, momentum=0.1) + ReLU`，超参和 `ResidualBlock` 的 `norm_fn` 保持一致。

**三步串联与超点聚合**：[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L358-L379](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L358-L379)——[L372-L374](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L372-L374) 依次过 `input_conv → unet → output_layer`；[L375](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L375) 用 `scatter_mean(x.features[inverse_mapping], superpoints)` 把体素特征按超点做均值池化；[L376-L378](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L376-L378) 按 `batch_offsets` 切回逐场景列表。

一个值得留意的分工细节：稀疏张量的**坐标/特征准备**用的是 MinkowskiEngine（`collate()` 里 `ME.TensorField` 与 `ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate`，[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L394-L411](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L394-L411)），而**卷积骨干**跑在 spconv 上（[L453-L454](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L453-L454) 构造 `spconv.SparseConvTensor`）。两个库各干各的活，靠 `(indices, features)` 这份共同语言衔接。

#### 4.4.4 代码实践

1. **实践目标**：亲手复现 `extract_feat` 的前三步（不含超点聚合），确认外壳与 U-Net 通道严丝合缝。
2. **操作步骤**（示例代码）：

```python
import torch, spconv.pytorch as spconv
from uniseg3d.spconv_unet import SpConvUNet

# 手工搭外壳（与 _init_layers 中的定义逐项等价，避免实例化整个 UniSeg3D）：
input_conv = spconv.SparseSequential(spconv.SubMConv3d(
    6, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1, bias=False, indice_key='subm1'))
output_layer = spconv.SparseSequential(
    torch.nn.BatchNorm1d(32, eps=1e-4, momentum=0.1), torch.nn.ReLU(inplace=True))

N = 5000
feats = torch.randn(N, 6)
idx = torch.cat([torch.zeros(N, 1, dtype=torch.int32),
                 torch.randint(0, 100, (N, 3), dtype=torch.int32)], dim=1)
x = spconv.SparseConvTensor(feats, idx, [100, 100, 100], batch_size=1)

unet = SpConvUNet([32 * (i + 1) for i in range(5)], return_blocks=True)
with torch.no_grad():
    h, _ = unet(input_conv(x))
    h = output_layer(h)
print('体素级特征:', tuple(h.features.shape))   # 期望 (5000, 32)
```

3. **需要观察的现象**：`input_conv` 后通道变 32、体素数不变；U-Net 输出仍为 `(5000, 32)`；`output_layer` 只改数值不改形状。
4. **预期结果**：最终打印 `(5000, 32)`，与 `extract_feat` 在 [uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L374](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L374) 处得到的张量规格一致。**待本地验证**。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

1. **练习**：`input_conv` 为什么选 `SubMConv3d` 而不是 `SparseConv3d`？
   **答案**：入口卷积只做 6→32 的通道升维，不应改变活跃点集合；`SubMConv3d` 保证输出位置与输入一致，后续 U-Net 第 1 级（以及共享的 `subm1` 规则表）才能在同一网格上工作。`SparseConv3d` 会做窗口扫描、改变活跃点集合，破坏这种对齐。
2. **练习**：如果把配置的 `num_channels` 从 32 改成 64，需要同步改动哪些地方才能保证前向不报错？
   **答案**：`num_planes` 由 `num_channels` 推导（配置 L37），U-Net 内部自动变宽；但 `output_layer` 的 `BatchNorm1d(num_channels)`、解码器侧消费的查询维度（`UnifiedQueryDecoder` 的 `in_channels`/`d_model` 相关设置）以及 `type_embedding` 的 `num_channels` 都依赖同一变量，而预训练权重（如 SSTNet `load_from`）的通道布局也须匹配——这正是配置用变量 `num_channels` 统一推导、而不是散落硬编码的原因。
3. **练习**：`output_layer` 里的 `BatchNorm1d(32)` 与 `ResidualBlock` 里的 `norm_fn` 有何异同？
   **答案**：都是对 `(N, C)` 的体素特征按通道归一化，超参一致（eps=1e-4, momentum=0.1）；区别只是定义位置——前者是主模型出口处的裸 `torch.nn.BatchNorm1d`，后者是作为 `functools.partial` 构造器贯穿所有残差块的默认 `norm_fn`。

## 5. 综合实践

**任务：为五级 SpConvUNet 绘制完整的「通道—体素数」数据流表，并验证递归自相似与外壳衔接。**

1. 把 4.2.4 的脚本与 4.3.4 的钩子探针合并：对同一个输入稀疏张量，先跑五级 `SpConvUNet(num_planes=[32*(i+1) for i in range(5)], return_blocks=True)`，把每个 `SparseSequential` 钩子的 `(name, 通道, 体素数)` 按执行顺序记录成表。

3. 再分别用 `num_planes=[32,64,96]` 与 `[32,64]` 重跑，确认表格结构按同一模式缩短（证明递归自相似），且最细层输出始终是 `(N, 32)`。
4. 最后套上 4.4.4 的 `input_conv`/`output_layer` 外壳，核对从 `(N, 6)` 进到 `(N, 32)` 出的完整链路，与 `extract_feat`（[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L372-L374](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L372-L374)）的调用顺序一致。
5. 预期产物：一张五级数据流表 + 一段结论（哪些层的体素数会变、哪些不变；哪些层共享 indice_key）。若本地无 GPU，全部步骤在 CPU 上即可完成；数值结果**待本地验证**。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `ResidualBlock` 是 pre-norm 残差块：`Norm → ReLU → SubMConv3d(3³) → Norm → ReLU → SubMConv3d(3³)` 加恒等分支（通道不等时用 1³ `SubMConv3d` 投影），全程不改变活跃点集合。
- `SpConvUNet` 通过 `self.u = SpConvUNet(num_planes[1:], indice_key_id+1, ...)` 递归自嵌套构建五级 U-Net；`num_planes=[32,64,96,128,160]`，每级「blocks → conv 下采样 → 递归 → deconv 上采样 → 跳连拼接 → blocks_tail」。
- `indice_key` 是 spconv 的规则表复用机制：同级 `SubMConv3d` 共享 `subm{i}`；`SparseInverseConv3d` 必须与配对的 `SparseConv3d` 共享 `spconv{i}`，从而把特征精确还原到下采样前的活跃点，使跳连拼接能逐行对齐。
- `return_blocks=True` 让 `forward` 返回 `(output, previous_outputs)`，多尺度列表由深到浅排列；但 `extract_feat` 用 `x, _ = self.unet(x)` 只消费 32 通道最细层输出。
- 外壳 `input_conv`（`SubMConv3d` 6→32，共享 `subm1`）与 `output_layer`（BN+ReLU）由主模型 `_init_layers` 搭建；体素级 32 维特征再经 `scatter_mean` 聚合成超点查询——「超点即查询」的原料在此产出。
- 坐标/特征准备用 MinkowskiEngine、卷积骨干用 spconv，两库以 `(indices, features)` 衔接。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

下一讲（u4-l3）顺着数据流进入 `uniseg3d/query_decoder.py`：看 32 维超点特征如何作为查询进入 `QueryDecoder` 的交叉注意力/自注意力/FFN 三件套，以及 `_forward_head` 如何用 einsum 点积生成掩码预测。建议先带着一个问题读：既然查询就是超点特征，解码器里的 `query_proj` 投影和 `attn_mask` 掩码分别解决什么？另外，若想巩固本讲的稀疏卷积直觉，可以对照 spconv 官方对 `SubMConv3d`/`SparseInverseConv3d` 的文档再看一遍 [uniseg3d/spconv_unet.py:L162-L199](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D/blob/c2729548d6f64122a92fce39b45d94b948782e67/uniseg3d/spconv_unet.py#L162-L199) 的 key 配对。

Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.
